subject: Hosted API evaluation follow-up — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeai.com>; Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation follow-up — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Sam / Lucy,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and clear next steps so your engineering team can kick off the hosted eval: 

1) Deployment fit: you mentioned wanting to start on Hosted API to accelerate integration and possibly migrate to Dedicated in 6–9 months as usage grows. That matches what we typically see (hosted for quick product validation, Dedicated when throughput/SLAs drive a commit).

2) Quickstart plan (what we'll do this week):
- Create a sandbox API key (scoped, 30-day) for your dev team.
- Provide a short quickstart guide (attached) showing the endpoints for generation, chat, and embeddings and example SDK calls.
- Set up a brief technical onboarding call (30m) with Marissa to walk your engineers through rate limits, batching, and metrics.

3) Hosted API endpoints & rate limits (defaults):
- POST /v1/generate — 60 requests/minute per API key (burst to 120 for 30s)
- POST /v1/chat — 40 requests/minute per API key
- POST /v1/embeddings — 120 requests/minute per API key (we optimize for batching)
- Token limits: 4,096 token context for standard hosted models; higher-context models available by request.

We can adjust rate limits for evaluation if needed — for example, we can enable a temporary higher-rate trial window for 24–72 hours. If you expect sustained higher QPS during the eval, let me know target numbers and we can provision.

4) Data & retention: Hosted API keeps request logs for 30 days by default for debugging; we offer options for shorter retention or enterprise retention policies on Dedicated/Private. If you need SOC2 evidence or specific retention terms for procurement, send over the questions and Marissa will route to Security.

Attachments: Redwood quickstart guide (PDF) and a short rate-limits spreadsheet.

Next steps:
- I’ll send the sandbox API key once you confirm which emails to provision keys for (dev@acmeai.com or the list below).
- Marissa will reach out to schedule the 30m tech onboarding.
- If procurement needs an intro for an NDA / SOW, I can loop in our contracts contact.

Thanks — happy to adjust the quickstart based on your stack.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172

---
Attachment: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
Attachment: hosted-api-rate-limits.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucy Park <lucy.park@acmeai.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation follow-up — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits

Thanks Aditya — really helpful summary. A couple quick questions before we spin up the sandbox keys: 

- Burst vs sustained: our initial integration will do a mix of single-turn chat (low QPS) and an embedding pipeline that batches ~500 docs per job. Can you confirm embedding throughput for batched requests (how many vectors per second for the hosted tier)?
- Tokens & costs: what’s the per-token billing for the standard hosted models vs an embeddings call?
- Rate limit overrides: if we ask for a temporary 72-hour higher QPS window for load testing, what’s the approval timeline?
- Data residency / retention: our legal/procurement will ask about data retention and deletion for hosted. Can you send the short SOC2/data handling summary so they can review?

We’re leaning toward Hosted for the proof-of-concept. If costs/throughput look good we’ll evaluate Dedicated in Q4. Please provision the sandbox key for dev@acmeai.com and include Lucy and me on the key usage.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme AI
sam.jenkins@acmeai.com

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick reply, answers below and next steps. Quoting your items to keep it clear.

> - Burst vs sustained: our initial integration will do a mix of single-turn chat (low QPS) and an embedding pipeline that batches ~500 docs per job. Can you confirm embedding throughput for batched requests (how many vectors per second for the hosted tier)?

For hosted tier: with batching (we recommend grouping up to 512 items per request) you should expect ~250–400 vectors/sec per API key for typical 1536-d embedding models. Throughput depends on average sequence length; if your docs are short (<=512 tokens) you’ll be at the higher end. For the eval I can enable a short higher-throughput window so you can validate end-to-end.

> - Tokens & costs: what’s the per-token billing for the standard hosted models vs an embeddings call?

Short answer: standard generation models are billed per input+output token; embeddings are billed per vector generation. I’m attaching the hosted-rate spreadsheet with the eval price tiers. For the sandbox eval we can set a temporary reduced rate so you can run benchmarks without incurring standard list pricing.

> - Rate limit overrides: if we ask for a temporary 72-hour higher QPS window for load testing, what’s the approval timeline?

We can typically enable a temporary increase within 24 business hours if you give target QPS numbers and the list of API keys to bump. For larger sustained increases we’d coordinate with Dedicated/reserved capacity planning.

> - Data residency / retention: our legal/procurement will ask about data retention and deletion for hosted. Can you send the short SOC2/data handling summary so they can review?

Marissa — can you drop the SOC2 summary and data handling bullet list to this thread? (Marissa: there’s also a short PDF in the shared drive I can link if helpful).

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Provision sandbox API key for dev@acmeai.com (temporary, will email credentials to dev+Lucy)
- Upload temporary higher-throughput config for a 48–72 hour window (please confirm target QPS if you want the full 72h)
- Marissa will send SOC2/data handling summary + schedule 30m onboarding for your engineering team.
- If procurement needs an NDA before we share more detailed security docs I can drop a DocuSign NDA link.

If this looks good I’ll provision the key and send creds later today.

Best,
Aditya Rao
